- [USER] User referenced three scholarly articles with specific details including authors, years, and URLs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Citation Success Index (CSI) is a metric for comparing the citation capacity of pairs of journals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The CSI is defined as the probability that a random paper in one journal has more citations than a random paper in another journal, with 50% indicating equal performance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The CSI differs from the journal impact factor (IF) as it depends on the broadness and shape of citation distributions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The CSI is a relatively tight function of the ratio of impact factors of journals being compared and grows slowly as a function of the impact factor ratio.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The lognormal distribution of citation counts explains the relationship between impact factors and the CSI.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The CSI was introduced in a paper by Stasa Milojevic and J. Bar-Ilan in 2016.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The CSI was further discussed in a 2017 paper by T. Milojevic and Judit Bar-Ilanb.
